name: Njalgulgule
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal. 2009. The modified form of Shatt Damam nouns and its Daju cognates. Afrika und Ubersee 88 (HAL halshs-00348145).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lists Njalgulgule among Daju languages only; sec. 2.3 prosody is about Shatt Damam ('two contrastive pitch levels.. not yet clear whether this prosodic system should be analyzed as tonal or as a stress system'). Nothing on Njalgulgule.

sources.citation: Thelwall, Robin. 1981. Lexicostatistical subgrouping and lexical reconstruction of the Daju group. In T. C. Schadeberg & M. L. Bender (eds.), Nilo-Saharan: Proceedings of the First Nilo-Saharan Linguistics Colloquium, Leiden 1980, 167-184. Dordrecht: Foris.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing (no occurrence of stress/accent/tone in the chapter). Njalgulgule appears only as five words from 'a Njalgulgule word list collected by Jon Arenson of SIL'; 'further data on Njalgulgule will not be included here but will appear in Thelwall 1981' (= the PhD thesis).

sources.citation: Santandrea, Stefano. 1948. Little known tribes of the Bahr el Ghazal basin. Sudan Notes and Records 29(1): 78-106; section 'The Njalgulgule -- a preliminary account', pp. 99-105.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The only phonology is p.105 'Phonetics. I simply record here my hurried impressions.' followed by segmental remarks (sh, kh, gh ~ Arabic 'ain/ghain, ny, ng, 'b, retroflex d; positional variation yokh ~ yohe 'husband'); editor's note says lines on sounds near 'ng' were omitted for lack of type. No mention of stress, accent or tone for Njalgulgule (the one accent/tone remark in the article, p.93, concerns the tribal names Biri/Viri vs. Bviri).

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal & Stefano Manfredi. 2014. Daju verbal morphology with special focus on Laggori and Shatt Damam (HAL hal-01102728, no file); Boyeldieu, P. comparative Daju lexicon (in prep.).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Most recent comparative Daju work; may summarise prosodic systems across the group and cite any Njalgulgule data beyond Santandrea/Arenson.
